Emeka Abernethy (Director of Operations): And I'm going to give you the numbers. Our current setup, we have about 162 people across five states, and last quarter we had 14 pay corrections out of roughly 1,900 paychecks. That's about 0.7 percent. Our target is under 0.3.
Rep: Okay. And after the demo, how did that look?
Emeka Abernethy (Director of Operations): Here's what moved me. I gave you three scenarios in advance. One was a clinician who works two locations in different states in the same pay period. Second was retroactive pay changes after a shift differential correction. Third was an approval flow where a manager is out. You ran all three with live data, not slides. Two of three matched what I'd expected. The third you said you'd get back on, and you did, in a day, with a screenshot.
Hollis Cadogan (General Manager): The part I cared about was the implementation. You laid out nine weeks, with two weeks of parallel payroll, and named who on our side owns each task. I counted eleven tasks, and I could see that eight were yours.
Emeka Abernethy (Director of Operations): Right. That was a differentiator for me. Our last vendor gave us a PDF with a Gantt chart nobody owned.
Rep: I'm glad that landed.
Hollis Cadogan (General Manager): We'd like to move forward. Can we target a go-live in the first pay cycle of January?
Rep: Working backward from that, we'd kick off the first week of November. I'll send the plan.
Emeka Abernethy (Director of Operations): Send it. I'll pressure test it.
